content: If someone is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. For other cases, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. In Canada, the number to call is 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests, such as kidney function and blood mineral levels, may be conducted to monitor your condition and ensure safety. It is important to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. For storage, refer to the instructions provided on the package label. If you have any questions about proper storage, consult your pharmacist. Do not freeze the medication, and avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. Please note that this is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. To use this medication, carefully read and follow all directions on the product package. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. To improve the taste, you may chill the product in the refrigerator before use, but do not freeze it. Mix your prescribed dose in 8 ounces (240 milliliters) of liquid and drink the solution. If your doctor has instructed you to use this product before surgery or a bowel procedure, follow their specific timing instructions closely. After taking the medication, drink plenty of clear fluids as directed by your doctor to prevent serious side effects such as kidney problems or dehydration. The dosage of this medication is determined based on your medical condition, the procedure being performed, your age, and your response to treatment. Do not take more of this medication than directed, use it more frequently than once in 24 hours, or use it for more than three days unless instructed by your doctor. Additionally, do not use other laxative products while taking this medication unless directed by your doctor. Prolonged or frequent use of this medication may lead to a condition known as laxative dependence, which can result in chronic constipation and loss of normal bowel function. For occasional constipation, a bulk-forming laxative (e.g., psyllium) or a stool softener (e.g., docusate) is generally a safer and more effective option. Mild side effects such as abdominal discomfort, cramps, gas, or nausea may occur. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Persistent diarrhea may lead to dehydration, which can cause serious complications for the kidneys and heart. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, do the same. Before taking sodium phosphate, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Consult your doctor before using this product if you have experienced a sudden change in bowel habits lasting more than two weeks or if you require a laxative daily for more than one week. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. The watery bowel movements caused by sodium phosphate may reduce the absorption of your regular medications, potentially decreasing their effectiveness. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, call 1-800-222-1222. In Canada, call 1-844-764-7669.
